sources.note: Removes external supervision from on-policy self-distillation by building a pseudo-solution from the model's own majority vote and using it as privileged teacher context rather than as a scalar reward, then distilling only on the completions that disagree with it.
sources.title: On-Policy Self-Distillation without Any Supervision

sources.note: Trains separate Top-K sparse autoencoders on a reasoning model's activations in thinking and non-thinking modes, and finds that suppressing the most active reasoning features destroys mathematical formatting as reliably as it destroys reasoning -- with the model responding by generating 454 percent more tokens of lower-diversity, more metacognitively marked text rather than stopping.
sources.title: Thinking vs. NoThinking: Towards Interpreting Reasoning Mechanisms of Large Language Models via Sparse Autoencoders

sources.note: Explores in weight space rather than token space during RLVR by sampling policies from a variational posterior at rollout time, and introduces a training-time exploration metric -- how often a method produces a correct rollout on a prompt where GRPO produced none -- because entropy and pass@k cannot tell exploration from degeneration.
sources.title: Parameter Exploration for RLVR via Variational Learning

sources.note: Identifies degenerate agreement -- students reaching near-perfect token agreement with a teacher by looping while the response as a whole is broken -- and replaces the agreement objective with two directional mismatch corrections, one bounding runaway excess tokens and one injecting teacher-preferred mass at positions the student almost never samples.
sources.title: Mismatch Matters: On-Policy Distillation Beyond Token Agreement

sources.note: Finds that a fact successfully unlearned from a multimodal model's final answer can still be reproduced in its reasoning trace, far more in natively RL-trained models than in their base versions, and uses the token-level entropy signature RL leaves behind as a training-free control signal for redirecting the trace at decoding time.
sources.title: LEMUR: Latent Entropy-aware Multimodal Unlearning via Visual-anchored Reasoning Redirection

result.definition: Output that satisfies a training or selection criterion while being useless -- repetition to the token limit, unterminated generation, loops that maximise agreement. Across 5 sources it is the concrete form the archive's local-metric warning takes. Its instances: a student reaching near-perfect token agreement with a teacher by looping while the response as a whole is broken; a reverse-KL objective collapsing by progressive loss of termination, with generations growing from 2.7 thousand characters to the token ceiling and parsable answers falling from 99 to 33 percent; a policy emitting repetitive tokens to an 8192-token limit under an unconstrained length reward; and a model whose most active reasoning features are suppressed responding by generating 454 percent more tokens of lower-diversity text rather than stopping. Two methodological consequences. Degenerate rollouts must be counted separately from incorrect ones, which one exploration metric does explicitly, because entropy and pass@k cannot distinguish exploration from degeneration. And a terminal check on the whole output is what separates degeneration from success, since every local metric in these cases was satisfied.
